event: 2026-08-26 Langtang Lirung ice-rock avalanche and Lhende Khola-Bhote Koshi-Trishuli debris flow
times: Nepal Standard Time (UTC+05:45) unless stated; compiled 2026-10-19
caveat: Many sources are secondary (Wikipedia, aggregators, news, NESRA). Primary NDRRMA/DHM/IFRC documents were mostly not accessible. Clock times for Dhunche, Trishuli Bazaar and hydropower sites could not be found.

timeline.what: Sentinel-1 InSAR records up to 40 cm line-of-sight deformation over 48 days; per ICIMOD not predictive of timing. Planet imagery of 12 and 25 Aug shows only minor change (Eos).
Tributary reaches 2.67 m vs 2.6 m threshold (rain-driven, unrelated to the later flood).
Seismic signals classified by ITP-CAS (preliminary, via Onlinekhabar); possibly early failure phases; not treated as precursors by the authors.

Daily bulletin flags significant Trishuli rise at Betrawati within two days and high flash-flood risk in small rivers of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha etc. (rain-based; no evidence it changed actions).
M2.6 tremor recorded.
Final border crossing logged on Nepal's e-immigration system.
Rock-ice slab collapses (seismic origin time 02:52 UTC); first reported as M4.4 earthquake, later USGS Ms 5.2 / GFZ Mw 5.7 landslide signal. Falls >1,200 m into Lhende Khola; 20-22 km in ~7 minutes.
Last reading 1.62 m (warning 6 m, danger 7 m).
CCTV captures start of destruction of the port (Wikipedia timeline); ICIMOD portal gives 08:40 for Rasuwagadhi arrival. Reconciled as 08:40-08:45.
Goes silent at 3.80 m (warning 5.5 m) per Spotlight Nepal; Wikipedia attributes the 1.62 m last reading to Syabrubesi instead (conflict; Spotlight chosen as more detailed).
Customs complex, Friendship Bridge, three police posts swept away. 32 police and 15 customs staff at Timure out of contact. 60 people out of contact at Langtang Khola hydropower (35 inside a tunnel).
Division learns of the flood by telephone (Rasuwa DAO and a Betrawati gauge staff member); confirmed 09:05. ~28 min after seismic signal.

SMS warnings via Nepal Telecom and Ncell to 679,295 recipients; ~38 min after collapse, ~25-30 min after Gyirong/Timure were hit. Evacuations start; a Nuwakot school moved ~900 children ~10 min before arrival.
Last level 3.55 m (warning 4.1, danger 5.0) then silent: ~43 min travel from border (~23 m/s).
No source found with clock arrival times for Dhunche or Trishuli Bazaar; Trishuli 3A/3B, Upper Trishuli and Devighat affected. Trishuli 3A tunnel later found flooded.
Flood forecast to reach Galchhi; high alert for Prithvi Highway and Muglin-Narayanghat road. Galchhi rose ~9 m in 30 min (press).
Warning level 11:20, danger 11:40; station and Phurke bridge swept away 11:43; alert reaches Malekhu >2 h after SMS wave began.
Flood passes Muglin; downstream appeals to Devghat.
Danger level crossed; peak 12.3-12.35 m (rating table ends at 10.9 m so no discharge).
Peak 6.57 m (est. ~5,850 m3/s), below its 7.3 m warning level; ~168 km from source; additional volume ~20 Mm3.
Activated at Nepal request (UNITAR); Sentinel Asia activated.
NDRRMA activated, 14 helicopters; IFRC releases ~CHF 1 million DREF; Nepal Red Cross deploys >200 staff/volunteers.
24-month Emergency Appeal for CHF 25 million announced (IFRC press release; appeal document dated 28 Aug; operation MDRNP022).

timeline.place: Barrier lakes (Chhochen Khola / Purepu Tsangpo confluence, TAR)
timeline.what: China warns a ~2 Mm3 barrier lake may breach; slight overflow 28 Aug (rise ~0.6 m per Nepal, level fall ~10 m per China); rescue paused ~3 h.
One lake draining, a second larger lake under assessment; Chinese statement 30-31 Aug that one lake near border fully drained.
~350 rescued, >100 still trapped in tunnel; Rasuwagadhi (111 MW) tunnel searched to ~225 m, ~93 workers missing.
Renewed rise (Galchhi ~+3 m); NDRRMA and DHM re-issue warnings.
Second event 7 weeks later: landslide, dam breach ~06:00, surge 20-25 m at Salleri; ~5 probable deaths; detected seismically; warnings reported effective.
Preliminary synthesis report launched: 132 Mm3, InSAR deformation, not a GLOF, calls for integrated satellite+seismic+hydrological monitoring and cross-border sharing.

summary.deaths_note: DPNet sitrep #2 chosen; early counts 8-9 dead, 19-20 missing

timeline.what: Supraglacial ponds grow from March; coalesce to single lake of 638,000 m2 on 7 July
First impact reported. Lake area falls to 435,000 m2. Flood travels ~35 km without intermediate ponding. Friendship Bridge destroyed, dry port severely damaged.
Early counts: 8-9 dead, 19-20 missing in Nepal and 11 on Chinese side; 57 rescued; Chinese workers among missing
DPNet situation report #2: 11 dead, 18 missing, 1 injured; ~1,950 security personnel deployed; damage to Friendship Bridge, Syabrubesi-Rasuwagadhi road, dry port, three hydropower plants, customs
None in place (RHA); cause confirmed later from satellite imagery; recurrence flagged as possible within 2025
